questions.question: Why does the Transformer use self-attention instead of recurrence?
questions.gold_supporting_passage: We propose a new simple network architecture, the Transformer, based solely on attention mechanisms, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions entirely.
questions.expected_facts: The Transformer is based solely on attention mechanisms and dispenses with recurrence and convolutions.

questions.expected_facts: The output is softmax(QK^T / sqrt(d_k))V.

questions.question: What does multi-head attention allow the model to attend to?
questions.gold_supporting_passage: Multi-head attention allows the model to jointly attend to information from different representation subspaces at different positions.
questions.expected_facts: It jointly attends to information from different representation subspaces at different positions.

questions.question: Why does the Transformer add positional encodings?
questions.gold_supporting_passage: Since our model contains no recurrence and no convolution, in order for the model to make use of the order of the sequence, we must inject some information about the relative or absolute position of the tokens in the sequence. To this end, we add "positional encodings" to the input embeddings at the bottoms of the encoder and decoder stacks.
questions.expected_facts: Because the model has no recurrence or convolution, positional information is injected into the input embeddings.

questions.question: What theoretical and practical latency does the Moshi paper report?
questions.gold_supporting_passage:
Our re-
sulting model is the first real-time full-duplex spoken large language model, with a theoret-
ical latency of 160ms, 200ms in practice, and is available at github.com/kyutai-labs/moshi.
questions.expected_facts: The paper reports 160 ms theoretical latency and 200 ms in practice.

questions.question: Why does Moshi model its own speech and the user's speech in parallel streams?
questions.gold_supporting_passage:
Moshi solves these independent issues altogether by casting spoken dia-
logue as speech-to-speech generation. Starting from a text language model backbone, Moshi
generates speech as tokens from the residual quantizer of a neural audio codec, while model-
ing separately its own speech and that of the user into parallel streams. This allows for the
removal of explicit speaker turns, and the modeling of arbitrary conversational dynamics.
questions.expected_facts: The parallel streams separately model Moshi's and the user's speech and support removing explicit speaker turns and modeling arbitrary conversational dynamics.

questions.question: How does Moshi's Inner Monologue method work?
questions.gold_supporting_passage: We insert W as the first sub-sequence in V , such that it acts as a prefix to the generation of semantic tokens.
questions.expected_facts: The text stream W is inserted as the first subsequence and acts as a prefix to semantic-token generation.

questions.question: What does the Dynamic Chunking paper say an H-Net replaces?
questions.gold_supporting_passage:
Incorporating this into an explicit hierarchical network (H-Net) allows replacing the (implicitly hierarchical) tokenization–LM–
detokenization pipeline with a single model learned fully end-to-end.
questions.expected_facts: An H-Net can replace the tokenization-LM-detokenization pipeline with one end-to-end learned model.

questions.question: Does the Dynamic Chunking paper say its learned chunking strategies require explicit supervision?
questions.gold_supporting_passage: H-Nets pretrained on English show significantly increased character-level robustness, and qualitatively learn meaningful data-dependent chunking strategies without any heuristics or explicit supervision.
questions.expected_facts: The paper says the learned data-dependent chunking strategies use neither heuristics nor explicit supervision.

questions.question: Moshi kya streaming ASR aur TTS provide kar sakta hai?
questions.gold_supporting_passage: We moreover extend the hierarchical semantic-to-acoustic token generation of previous work to first predict time-aligned text tokens as a prefix to audio tokens. Not only this “Inner Monologue” method significantly improves the linguistic quality of generated speech, but we also illustrate how it can provide streaming speech recognition and text-to-speech.
questions.expected_facts: The paper illustrates that Inner Monologue can provide streaming speech recognition and text-to-speech.

questions.question: Does Dynamic Chunking prove that H-Nets are better than every tokenized model in every setting?
questions.gold_supporting_passage: When compute- and data- matched, an H-Net with one stage of hierarchy operating at the byte level outperforms a strong Transformer language model operating over BPE tokens.
questions.expected_facts: The paper reports an advantage in the stated compute- and data-matched comparison, not a universal result for every tokenized model or setting.

questions.question: Does Moshi's full-duplex design guarantee that every real conversation will have no interruptions?
questions.gold_supporting_passage: This altogether removes the concept of speaker turn and thus allows training the model on natural conversations with arbitrary dynamics including overlap and interruptions.
questions.expected_facts: The paper says the design removes the concept of speaker turns and allows training on conversations with overlap and interruptions; it does not guarantee that all real interruptions are eliminated.

questions.question: Kya Moshi har conversational interruption ko eliminate karne ka proof deta hai?
questions.gold_supporting_passage: This allows for the removal of explicit speaker turns, and the modeling of arbitrary conversational dynamics.
questions.expected_facts: The paper supports removal of explicit speaker turns and modeling arbitrary dynamics, but does not prove that every interruption is eliminated.

questions.question: Kya Dynamic Chunking Chinese ke har task par tokenized models se better hai?
questions.gold_supporting_passage:
Finally, the H-Net’s improvement over tokenized pipelines is further increased in languages and modalities with weaker tokenization heuristics, such as Chinese
and code, or DNA sequences (nearly 4× improvement in data efficiency over baselines), showing the potential of true
end-to-end models that learn and scale better from unprocessed data.
questions.expected_facts: The paper reports increased improvement in settings such as Chinese with weaker tokenization heuristics; it does not establish superiority on every Chinese task.

questions.question: Does the sinusoidal positional encoding guarantee that a Transformer will extrapolate to any longer sequence?
questions.gold_supporting_passage: We chose this function because we hypothesized it would allow the model to easily learn to attend by relative positions, since for any fixed offset k, PEpos+k can be represented as a linear function of PEpos. We also experimented with using learned positional embeddings [9] instead, and found that the two versions produced nearly identical results (see Table 3 row (E)). We chose the sinusoidal version because it may allow the model to extrapolate to sequence lengths longer than the ones encountered during training.
questions.expected_facts: The authors hypothesize that sinusoidal encodings may allow extrapolation; the passage does not guarantee extrapolation to any length.
